answer: No, they do not cover the same set of persons. The original definition of 'representative' was limited to 'an employee or an agent of an investment adviser who renders investment advice on behalf of that investment adviser.' The 2020-amended definition of 'persons associated with investment advice' is broader: it covers 'any member, partner, officer, director or employee or any sales staff' including 'any person occupying a similar status or performing a similar function irrespective of the nature of association' who is 'engaged in providing investment advisory services to the clients.' The explanation further clarifies that all client-facing persons (e.g., service relationship managers, client relationship managers) are included, while only persons discharging purely clerical or office administrative functions with no client interface are excluded. Thus the 2020 definition captures a wider group than the original.

answer: No, they do not describe the same type of professional. An 'independent research analyst' is a person whose ONLY business activity is research analysis or preparation and/or publication of research reports. A 'part-time research analyst' is an individual or a partnership firm who, for consideration, is engaged in providing research services AND is also engaged in any other business activity or employment. The key distinction is that an independent research analyst has no other business activity, while a part-time research analyst also has other business or employment.
